reason: Under the schedule and feasibility lens the idea survives: it can be built and scored well before 29 Sep 10:00 UTC. It passes only as a rider, because no LB probe can resolve it. (1) Implementable as described. Checked in experiments/exp56_x138_verbatim/exp56-x138-verbatim.ipynb, which is x138 byte-identical. In cell 4, the 'lowdet peaks' replacement dumps _low from _detect_cells_pooled at BIOHUB_LOWDET_THRESHOLD=0.3 (cell 0; not 0.5 as the idea says, so the head runs on the >=0.3 pool). _lsc is gathered at the integer indices. 'lowdet write' multiplies by downsample and then casts to int16. ds_path, t, unet_out and f_idx are all in scope there, because x138's own V1284 line uses them one line later. The refine module is stateless apart from the cached head weights. Its shift is bounded at 2 um, and it raises only above 2.00001 um, which cannot happen by construction. Cell 5 reads low_coords as float64 and uses vox only via float(...), with no integer indexing, so a float32 dump is safe. (2) The idea's numbers check out. 1,337/121,777 = 1.1% readmitted (CONTEXT 08:40). READMIT_MIN_SCORE 0.965 = the detector threshold, so readmitted nodes are main-pool peaks that the ILP dropped. They already had refined coordinates before the ILP, and the fix restores exactly those. The head bound is 2 um and GAPFILL_EXCLUDE_UM is 2.0 (a peak is free only at d > 2), so every unrefined main copy is already excluded today. The fix makes that distance exactly 0 and cannot change the exclusion. (3) No runtime risk: the extra cost is a 7-offset feature gather plus a 224->32->3 MLP on the >=0.3 peaks, about seconds per movie (guess: < 1 min per run). That is negligible against the 27,000 s runtime guard (REPAIR_DEADLINE_S) and the 12 h limit. (4) Two traps (x122 failure mode): the refine call must come AFTER _lsc, and the replacement must not add a second 'coord_offset[t] = ...' line, because the V1284 patch requires that anchor count to be exactly 1. (5) The real weakness under this lens is statistical power, not the calendar. Expected effect: +0.0002 (value sibling v_redteam-past_refine-lowdet-peaks-x138_value.json). LB noise is 0.003 and the display step 0.001. A dedicated slot would be scored on time but would measure nothing, so it should never get its own slot.
fix_if_any: Build it as tools/build_probe_kernel.py --base x138 --patch lowdetrefine (a new patch; --base x138 currently allows only divinsert and leafprune). Knob BIOHUB_LOWDET_REFINE default 0. Inside the 'lowdet peaks' new-string, right after _lsc: if knob, _low = _v1284_refine(ds_path, t, _low, unet_out[:, f_idx]). In 'lowdet write', skip the astype(np.int16) when the knob is on (the empty case can stay int16). Do not emit an extra coord_offset line. Checks: knob=0 output CSV byte-identical to out_exp56. With knob=1 on the 4 dummy clips: readmitted and gap-fill peak counts within +-10% per clip; no REPAIR FAILED; 'Low-detection dump applied' and 'V1284 head patched' both printed; LOWDET peak counts unchanged. Ship only inside an x138-based bundle that is scored anyway (e.g. exp57b-type insertion or idea 1), and never attribute a LB delta to it.
realistic_public_gain: +0.0002 (0 .. +0.0005; from the value sibling). Unmeasurable: LB noise 0.003, display step 0.001.
realistic_private_gain: +0.0002 (-0.0002 .. +0.0005). Nothing leans on network confidence, so it transfers as well as public, but it is equally negligible.
critical_path: Step 0, 25 Sep 11:00-17:00 UTC (no GPU needed): the agent container writes the lowdetrefine patch for --base x138, adds the knob, checks with compile() and runs the anchor-count asserts (~1-1.5 h). Step 1, 25 Sep 17:00-20:00 UTC: #34/#35 score and decide the host base (x138 if #34 ~0.953; P about 0.85, guess, since 41 teams reproduce 0.953). If #34 falls short, the rider can still go on any x138-based build, or be dropped with no loss. Step 2, 26 Sep ~06:00-08:00 UTC: Vitalii pushes the kernel and runs the private 4-clip dummy test on Kaggle vitaliineibauer (GPU quota reset at 26 Sep 00:00 UTC; 15-40 min T4, ~0.7 GPU-h of 30). That window is the realistic human-awake one (guess; team appears MSK-based). The byte-identity (knob=0) and count checks are done on the downloaded outputs by the agent (~20 min). Friend A / sasyami is not needed. Step 3, 26 Sep ~08:30-09:30 UTC: with the user's explicit OK it goes into the day's x138-based bundle, using no extra slot (5 slots on 26 Sep). Step 4: scored ~15:30-19:30 UTC 26 Sep (7-10 h latency; runtime about x138's plus < 1 min). Slack to the 29 Sep 10:00 UTC cutoff: ~2.5 days, with room for 2 retries on 27 and 28 Sep. P(scored | team decides to ship it) ~0.9. The binding risk is a team decision, not time: the value sibling refuted it at +0.0002, so it may never be shipped. Even when scored, the result cannot be attributed.
